item.title: Hump-nosed Pit Viper <Hypnale hypnale> feeding on an Allapalli Skink Eutropis allapallensis in Karwar, India
item.description: We report a probable first case of in situ field observation of a wild Hump-nosed Pit Viper Hypnale hypnale hunting and feeding. This is based on a direct observation involving an Allapalli Skink Eutropis allapallensis that occurred on 23 May 2024, at 2200 h in Karwar, India. The entire event lasted for 6 m 40 s, while the skink became immobile, eventually died out of envenomation in just 40 s after fang-contact.

item.title: Record of <Euploea mulciber> (Cramer, [1777]) (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in Delhi, India: evidence of range extension in a restored urban ecosystem
item.description: This study documents the first records of the Striped Blue Crow butterfly, Euploea mulciber, in Delhi, India, observed within the Aravalli Biodiversity Park in 2013, 2018, and 2022. item.title: A note on the Petal-less Caper <Maerua apetala> (B.Heyne ex Roth) Jacobs (Capparaceae)
item.description: The Petal-less Caper Maerua apetala (B.Heyne ex Roth) Jacobs (= Capparis apetala B.Heyne ex Roth) is a large-canopied but short dry evergreen tree, endemic to southeastern India. item.title: Community structure of Lepidoptera in Nantu-Boliohuto Wildlife Reserve, Sulawesi, Indonesia
item.description: Lepidoptera diversity serves as a vital bioindicator of ecosystem health and environmental quality. item.title: Comparing three sampling techniques for surveying and monitoring arthropods in Moroccan agroecosystems
item.description: Insect monitoring is a key component of sustainable and productive crop management. Among the various methods used to observe insect communities, pitfall trapping, visual searching, and sweep-net sampling of vegetation are the most widely applied. Selecting an appropriate sampling method is essential to obtain a comprehensive and accurate representation of species diversity. item.title: Assessing the tree diversity along the Dudhganga River in Kolhapur District of Maharashtra, India
item.description: Riparian vegetation is the buffer zone between the aquatic ecosystem of a river and the terrestrial ecosystem. Trees are a typical feature of many ecosystems. item.title: Floristic composition and conservation significance of vascular plants in Kalatop-Khajjiar Wildlife Sanctuary, Himachal Pradesh, India
item.description: Kalatop–Khajjiar Wildlife Sanctuary represents one of the ecologically significant forested landscapes of the northwestern Himalaya; however, updated and systematic documentation of its vascular flora has remained limited.
